brief: Mideast escalation - US strikes on Iranian crude carriers, an Iranian strike on a US base in Jordan and on shipping near Hormuz, and Houthi attacks on Saudi refining - pushed Brent above $101, near July highs, and drove short-end yields higher early. Long-end yields then snapped higher after Treasury's enlarged buyback (at least $4bn committed, $6bn delivered versus an $8-10bn whisper) disappointed on size, even though the 10Y auction traded well. Yields closed higher with a bear steepening, 2Y outperforming the belly. Markets are pricing a 62% chance of a hike at next week's FOMC. US equities fell broadly, led by small caps as a most-shorted-stock squeeze unwound, breadth staying weak. Bear Traps Report's Lawrence McDonald counted nine Hindenburg Omen triggers in 30 sessions, a count Tom McClellan disputed, putting his stricter-rule total at four. Bitcoin closed flat near $78,600 but formed a Golden Cross for the first time in 474 days, a pattern the note says preceded 3-month gains above 40% in each of the last five instances. Gold rose above $4400. The dollar ended flat as Bessent threatened yen shorts while the yen kept appreciating on BOJ-tightening expectations, flagged as a risk of yen-carry unwind hitting equities.
